terra.problem: The text does not say Ahab kept pointing at the city, that sheep and cattle were on a table, or that he urged Jehoshaphat right after a feast. It also does not say the welcome had strings attached.
“Wrong map” uses “wrong” about the baker’s answer.
The drawer joke suggests Papa could have checked something before spending years there. He was put in the drawer; he did not choose to sit there.
The angel and junk drawer joke relies on Papa’s backstory without explaining that an angel called him out of the drawer. It also treats an angel as a show.
“Wrong metal, wrong animal” uses “wrong” about the baker’s answer. The claim that a bronze serpent is elsewhere in the Bible also needs a reference.
The text says the prophets spoke favorably, but does not say they were lining up to say what the king wanted.
The text does not say the other prophets spoke whatever the king told them.
“He listens politely” adds a manner the text does not give.
The vision describes Israel as scattered like sheep without a shepherd. It does not say there was a literal flock without a leader, or that the people were wandering.
The vision does not say nobody was carrying loot.
The vision does not say nobody was holding a post.
The explanation states that Ahab was hoping to win without marking that feeling as Papa’s guess.
The spirit’s account explains the lying message, but the text does not say it explains why the prophets sounded sure.
The explanation calls the Spirit of the LORD “it,” although the passage refers to the Spirit as “He.”
“Who ends up hiding” presents Micaiah’s prediction as an event that has already happened.
The passage says an inner room, not that its door is shut.
“Not even close” is a negative response to the baker’s answer.
Calling Micaiah’s statement a bet on his own word obscures his claim that the LORD had spoken through him.
